notable_absence.finding: This archive page documents dozens of API-shape changes across seven alpha/beta releases (e.g. JCBC-1497 'All deprecated APIs are removed', JCBC-1512 'ExpandMacro is gone', JVMCBC-731 'the CAS-based observe has been removed', JCBC-1355 'Spatial view API support has been removed since it is deprecated on the server') that would, on a GA release, be exactly the removedIn/deprecatedIn shape. None were captured as relations here: every one of these describes an unreleased, unsupported pre-GA API surface churning between alpha/beta builds rather than a real API a user could have been depending on, and the page itself states 'none of the pre-releases listed below are supported'. Treating alpha-to-alpha churn as removedIn facts would flood the registry with version-gated claims about an API shape that never shipped.

cross_component_finding: JCBC-1355's 'Spatial view API support has been removed since it is deprecated on the server' is a real, still-true cross-component fact (the Java SDK dropping a client API in step with server-side Spatial View deprecation) but the quote gives no version number for either side, so it cannot be expressed as a dated removedIn/deprecatedIn relation without fabricating a version. Left uncaptured for the same reason as the notable_absence above - better to omit than to guess a version.
cross_product_finding: This page's only substantive, still-true facts (JVMCBC-694 cluster-level queries without an open bucket, JVMCBC-729 the query-prepare mechanism) are both gated on Couchbase Server 6.5 and later - not on Couchbase Java SDK 3.0 itself. Neither is worth restating in the 3.0 GA release notes because they're Server capabilities, not SDK-version-specific ones - consistent with this round's framing that Server-version facts and the SDK's own 3.x.y version numbering are two independent axes.
